newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court cases signal Rao's political eclipse.
newsitem.headline: Indian court cases signal Rao's political eclipse.

text.p: India's Congress party paid homage to Indira Gandhi on her death anniversary on Thursday, but its leaders said their gloom was rivetted on the imminent political eclipse of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.
Gandhi, who gave Rao his first cabinet job in 1980, was assassinated by two Sikh bodyguards on October 31 1984. She was India's only prime minister for 16 years.

Rao, 75, became India's first former or serving prime minister to face a criminal trial when he appeared on Wednesday in a heavily guarded court room to hear charges of forgery related to a 1989 case.
Adding to his woes, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Wednesday slapped a fresh charge of bribery on Rao in a case in which he is accused of using money to win a trust vote in parliament.
"There is no denying the fact that this has harmed the party," Congress president Sitaram Kesri told reporters on Thursday about Rao's growing list of criminal charges.
Kesri took over the badly divided party last month as a compromise leader after the CBI named Rao in a 1983 cheating case and he resigned as Congress president.

"When I met him two months ago, Rao told me he wanted to leave the party leadership but he was worried about the fate of the Congress without him," political columnist Kuldip Nayar told Reuters on Thursday.

"I don't think he was ready to believe that he himself was responsible for bringing the party to such a sorry pass," Nayar said. "But we all know that this is the begining of his fading out from politics."

Rao led the Congress to its worst ever defeat in the March/April general elections this year that returned a hung parliament. The party's downfall was then blamed largely on several corruption cases against Rao's cabinet colleagues.
But Rao maneouvred the Congress to keep the balance of power in the new government when he promised support to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's left-leaning United Front minority alliance.
The beleaguered former premier has so far retained the key leadership of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP), a post politicians said could soon be taken away from him.
Kesri has called a meeting of the decision-making Congress Working Committee on November 4 where, his aides say, he would review the party's support to Deve Gowda and Rao's leadership of the CPP.
"Kesri has already signalled his intentions by removing Rao's pictures from the party's street posters," a Congress politician said.
"But there is feeling of a vacuum at the top. He has installed Indira Gandhi's pictures in place of Narasimha Rao. But she is dead and he is in deep trouble."
Rao's aides say the former premier was hurt by what he feels was a systematic effort by his colleagues to sideline him.
"He exudes this sense of betrayal," Nayar said. "He names names, and says so-and-so had let him down for no fault of his."
Analysts say Rao's 1991-96 rule would be best remembered for his sweeping economic reforms. But there, too, Rao attracted some unexpected criticism this week.
"I was a junior commerce minister in the previous government so I was party to its decisions," Finance Minister P. Chidmabaram told a New Delhi business seminar early this week.

"But it is a fact that (Rao's) focused effort to bring down the inflation to a record 4.5 percent was also responsible for a squeeze on money supply. And that is having its negative impact today," Chidmabaram said.
